decision.notes: Everything else looks right: the status classification, kind-only IPC, the macOS argv passing and the Linux positional args. The fix is confined to the Windows sign-in launch.
reasons: c2 not met, a command injection on Windows. planWindows builds `start "Sign in" cmd.exe /d /v:off /s /k ""<path>" <login>"` and runs it through an outer `cmd.exe /s /c`. At the outer level the quotes toggle 4 times before the path ("Sign in", then ""), so the path is UNQUOTED there and an `&` in it ends the command. Reproduced: with `echo` in place of `start` and the path `C:\a & echo INJECTED & b\x.cmd`, the output contains INJECTED on its own line. A folder such as `tools & calc & x` holding claude.cmd would run calc. DM-47 explicitly supports `&` in paths, so it can't simply be refused.

Fix: don't route the path through two cmd parses. For example, spawn the console directly: `spawn(comspec, ['/d','/v:off','/s','/k', '""<path>" <login args>"'], { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore', windowsVerbatimArguments: true, windowsHide: false })`. That gives a new visible console with exactly one cmd parse, as in DM-47's probe, and you can set the title with `title` only if you keep it a constant prefix inside that one parse. Or otherwise prove the path is literal in every cmd parse it passes through.

Add a test that shows it: an agentAuthNode-style test that runs the exact planned Windows command line through cmd.exe with a harmless stand-in for the window launch (e.g. echo, or a fake .cmd in a directory named like `x & echo INJECTED & y`), and asserts nothing was injected. outputs.summary:
A hosted Claude chat now asks before any write into a Claude Code memory folder. The fix has two parts, both passed in the SDK query options; no settings file is read or written.

1. A PreToolUse hook (matcher Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit). For a target that resolves into `<config dir>/projects/*/memory/` it answers `permissionDecision: 'ask'`, and the CLI then calls the app's canUseTool, so the write becomes an ordinary file_edit card. This was proven live in SDK 0.3.289 and CLI 2.1.281, including over a blanket Write allow rule.
   - Path matching (claudeMemoryFolder.ts): `~` is expanded; relative paths are resolved against the chat folder and the reported cwd; `..` is folded; either slash is accepted; matching is case- and NFC-insensitive; on Windows the `\\?\` prefix, trailing dots or spaces and ADS suffixes are dropped; links and junctions are followed through realpath of the nearest existing ancestor; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is honoured and ~/.claude is always covered. An unreadable call fails closed (asks).
2. An inline `settings: { autoMemoryDirectory: <tmp>/dark-mechanicus-unused-memory }`, which the SDK passes as `--settings`. This moves the CLI's own memory carve-out to a folder nothing reads, so a shell redirect into a real memory folder asks by the CLI's own rules. The worker found that hole live: 'shell commands already ask' was false.

Sources: sdk.d.ts (hooks line 1730, HookCallbackMatcher 971, PreToolUseHookSpecificOutput 2748, Options.settings 2212, Settings.autoMemoryDirectory 9130), and code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, /settings (precedence) and /memory.

Live results, from the real adapter bundle against claude.exe 2.1.281 on Haiku: absolute, ~, relative (six ..), forward slashes, upper case, through a junction, editing an existing file, and shell redirects (>>, 1>>, >, a relative target, through the junction) each raised a card, and on Deny the folder listing was unchanged. Allow wrote the file, and an ordinary write still asks. The controls without the fix wrote silently.
